description:
About Us

We are MIRI STYLE, a passionate 4-member team participating in the Sarawak Space Challenge 2026! We are taking on the "Dancing with the SARs" challenge. Our group brings together a creative mix of interests in Earth science, radar remote sensing, data visualization, and interactive app design to track Earth's surface changes.
summary:
During the winter monsoon, continuous heavy rain causes severe flooding across the coastal town of Miri. Low-lying neighborhoods and roads near sea level can cut off travel and is worsened by blocked drainage. It also triggers landslides like the collapse near Bintang Megamall during January of this year. Sometimes heavy rain does not cause flooding due to factors like low soil moisture or tidal levels. Because thick storm clouds block regular satellites, early warning is difficult.

For the Dancing with SARs challenge, we built a website that uses NISAR, which sees through clouds to help research and monitor soil moisture around Miri. By comparing multi-date images over time, our platform shows how soil around Miri become saturated before heavy rain arrives. When soil is already heavily saturated, floods can become more extreme. We turn complex NASA-ISRO radar imagery into a simple timeline to help Miri communities prepare.
details:
AquaSAR is a web-based tool that visualizes soil moisture using NASA-ISRO SAR imagery data.

What it does / How it works:

AquaSAR reads NISAR backscatter values from 0.08 (-11dB) to 0.20 (-7dB). Weak backscatter (blue,0.08) indicates smooth, wet surfaces like water, while strong backscatter (red, ∼0.20) indicates rough surfaces like forest and buildings. When soil that is brown on imagery becaomes loght green or yellow, it indicates the soil being saturated with water .Our website lets users view this data on an interactive map with a compare slider, e.g., 5 Sept 2025 vs 17 Sept 2025 over Miri, Sarawak, showing how backscatter changes every 12 days as soil conditions change.

Benefits:

It turns complex SAR data into a simple color map that anyone in Miri can understand. Instead of raw monochrome images, citizens can read the images and be prepared for a incoming flood.

Intended Impact:

Today, AquaSAR maps soil moisture. Tomorrow, it can help the people of Miri prepare before a flood comes by identifying saturated areas early. It also gives Miri a long-term tool to monitor its changing ecosystems, with potential to scale to other cities with NISAR data available.

Tools Used:

Under space apps respurces:ASF Data Search Vertex, NISAR Data Guide, Intro to Remote Sensing, Intro to SAR's

AI used: Chatgpt, Claude, Gemini, Lovable

Creativity & Factors Considered:

We focused on making SAR data easily-readable using a blue-to-red scale and a swipe comparison intead of monochrome colours which dB values are hard to differentiate. We considered local relevance, our hometown, Miri being a coastal city, and the outskirts of Miri mostly being plantations which has many soil. We hope the website can keep citizens well prepared for an incoming flood, and to prevent any tragic deaths caused by the natural disaster, such as the case in January 2025 where a landslide happened at Lereng Bukit causing the unfortunate deaths of 5 people.
